assumptions: no observed macro dataset supplied; all values are heuristic priors
subdomain of Money, Banking & Macro-Finance scoped to reading the macro picture money operates in
nodes are concrete explanatory work-units for reading the macroeconomy, not full forecasting models
key references are Mankiw Macroeconomics and Eichengreen Globalizing Capital

competency_questions.question: Which macro question (cyclical vs structural, nominal vs real, domestic vs external) is being read and over what horizon?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MACRO_SCOPE_FRAME and MACRO_SYNTHESIS define and integrate the question

competency_questions.question: Which aggregates answer the scoped question and how do they map to it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: scope frame links to GDP and inflation aggregates

competency_questions.question: How is aggregate output measured and how reliable are its vintages?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GDP and data-quality nodes answer measurement and reliability

competency_questions.question: Is observed inflation driven by supply or demand and is it transitory or persistent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: inflation and shock nodes plus the gap-inflation axis resolve this

competency_questions.question: Are inflation expectations anchored and what would signal de-anchoring?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: expectations node and its edges define anchoring and de-anchoring

competency_questions.question: How much slack or overheating exists and how does it map to inflation pressure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: output-gap, labor, and Phillips nodes link slack to inflation

competency_questions.question: Which business-cycle phase is the economy in and how confident is the call?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: dating and leading-indicator nodes answer phase and confidence

competency_questions.question: What forward signals anticipate a turning point and how reliable are their lead times?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: leading-indicator node and its dating edge answer lead reliability

competency_questions.question: Where is real-time data reliability weakest and how should it temper confidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: data-quality node and its constraint edges temper confidence

competency_questions.question: How do shocks, policy, and external factors reconcile into one coherent macro narrative?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: synthesis node integrates shocks, policy, and external reads

competency_questions.question: Is the monetary and fiscal policy mix tight or loose relative to the cycle and what is the mix tension?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: policy nodes and the policy-mix conflict axis answer stance and tension

competency_questions.question: What is the fiscal stance, multiplier size, and its effect on the gap and debt?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: fiscal, multiplier, and debt nodes answer stance through to debt

competency_questions.question: Is the public debt path sustainable given r minus g and rollover risk?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: debt-sustainability node and its conflict edges answer the path

competency_questions.question: How do exchange rates, the external balance, and capital flows affect domestic inflation and stability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: external-block nodes answer the external transmission

glossary.definition: actual minus potential output as a share of potential
inflation excluding volatile food and energy components
the relationship between economic slack and inflation
the gap between the interest rate on debt and the growth rate
the share of an exchange-rate move that reaches domestic prices
the degree to which inflation expectations stay near target
an abrupt reversal of capital inflows
a disturbance shifting aggregate supply and moving output and prices oppositely
the real interest rate consistent with stable inflation at potential output
the fiscal balance net of the business cycle

evidence_label_policy.rationale: no observed or experimental evidence supplied; all estimates are heuristic priors referencing SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from standard macroeconomics texts (Mankiw Macroeconomics; Eichengreen Globalizing Capital) and established macro practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

nodes.definition: Defines which macro question is being read (cyclical vs structural, nominal vs real, domestic vs external) and the aggregates that answer it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: macro question reframed from cyclical to structural or horizon changes

pros.claim: frames every downstream aggregate and policy read
pros.example: typing the question first avoids mistaking a supply shock for a demand cycle

cons.claim: over-framing can exclude relevant aggregates
cons.example: narrow nominal framing missed real-wage erosion in the 2021-22 inflation read

acceptance_tests: question type horizon and nominal real status are explicit and mutually consistent
aggregate shortlist maps to the stated question

nodes.definition: Measures aggregate output via expenditure income and production identities and the C plus I plus G plus NX accounting frame.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark revision or rebasing of national accounts

pros.claim: anchors output gap growth and per-capita welfare reads
pros.example: the C I G NX identity isolates which demand component drove a slowdown

cons.claim: GDP omits non-market and distributional detail
cons.example: headline growth hid stagnant median income

nodes.definition: Measures the rate of change of a price level via index construction CPI PCE core and decomposes headline vs underlying inflation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: index methodology change substitution-bias evidence or core headline divergence

pros.claim: separates transitory base effects from persistent trend
pros.example: trimmed-mean inflation revealed broadening 2022 price pressure beneath volatile energy

cons.claim: index choice and substitution bias bias the level
cons.example: CPI overstated cost-of-living relative to PCE in some periods

acceptance_tests: headline decomposed into core plus volatile components
base effects explicitly netted out

nodes.definition: Measures labor-market slack via unemployment rate participation U6 and vacancy quits to read how tight the economy runs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: definitional change to participation or vacancy data revision

pros.claim: tightness drives wage and inflation pressure reads
pros.example: a high vacancy-to-unemployment ratio signaled 2022 wage acceleration

cons.claim: headline rate hides discouraged workers and underemployment
cons.example: low U3 masked weak participation after 2020

nodes.definition: Estimates the gap between actual and potential output to gauge cyclical slack or overheating and inflation pressure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: potential-output re-estimate or end-of-sample filter revision

pros.claim: links real activity to inflation pressure via Phillips logic
pros.example: a positive gap warned of building 2022 price pressure

cons.claim: potential output is unobservable and revised heavily at the end of sample
cons.example: real-time gap estimates flipped sign after revision

acceptance_tests: gap reported with explicit uncertainty band
method filter vs production function stated

nodes.definition: Identifies expansion peak recession and trough phases using coincident indicators and turning-point rules.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: official dating-committee revision or indicator methodology change

pros.claim: phase label conditions which policy and forecast logic applies
pros.example: early recession dating reframed 2008 policy urgency

cons.claim: turning points are confirmed with a lag
cons.example: a two-quarter rule mislabeled non-recessionary slowdowns

nodes.definition: Uses forward-looking indicators yield curve PMI claims LEI and nowcasts to anticipate turning points.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: indicator lead-lag relationship breaks down or false-signal cluster appears

pros.claim: buys lead time before official dating
pros.example: yield-curve inversion preceded several US recessions

cons.claim: indicators give false positives and unstable lead times
cons.example: the inversion signal misfired around the mid-2020s soft-landing debate

nodes.definition: Classifies shocks as supply vs demand and tracks their distinct effects on output and prices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: shock-source reattribution between supply and demand given new sectoral evidence

pros.claim: the supply vs demand sign determines whether policy should lean against output or prices
pros.example: the 2021-22 debate hinged on the supply-shock vs demand-overheating share

cons.claim: shocks are mixed and identification is contested
cons.example: mislabeling supply inflation as demand raised over-tightening risk

acceptance_tests: price-output co-movement used to justify the shock sign
persistence horizon stated

nodes.definition: Reads how a central bank uses policy rates balance sheet and guidance to affect demand inflation and expectations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: policy framework change such as average inflation targeting or transmission evidence

pros.claim: the rate path and guidance steer demand and the inflation path
pros.example: the 2022-23 hiking cycle aimed to re-anchor expectations

cons.claim: transmission acts with long variable lags
cons.example: premature easing risks re-igniting inflation

acceptance_tests: stance judged against an explicit rule benchmark
transmission-lag horizon stated

nodes.definition: Reads how government spending and taxation change aggregate demand the cyclically-adjusted stance and automatic stabilizers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cyclically-adjusted balance re-estimate or large discretionary package

pros.claim: it separates the active stance from automatic-stabilizer movement
pros.example: the cyclically-adjusted balance distinguished stimulus from a recession-driven deficit

cons.claim: the headline deficit conflates cycle and policy
cons.example: the raw deficit overstated discretionary easing in downturns

nodes.definition: Estimates the output response per unit of fiscal change accounting for crowding-out slack-dependence and monetary offset.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence on state-dependent multiplier size or monetary-offset regime

pros.claim: multiplier size flips the cost-benefit of stimulus
pros.example: slack-state multipliers above one justified the 2009 stimulus framing

cons.claim: multipliers are regime-dependent and hard to pin
cons.example: applying recession-era multipliers at full employment overstated stimulus benefit

nodes.definition: Assesses whether the public debt path is stable using the debt dynamics identity r minus g primary balance and rollover risk.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: shift in the r minus g sign term-premium repricing or rollover-stress evidence

pros.claim: the r minus g sign determines whether debt stabilizes without austerity
pros.example: negative r minus g eased post-2010 sustainability fears for some sovereigns

cons.claim: r and g are jointly uncertain and can shift fast
cons.example: assuming permanently low r understated rollover risk when rates rose

acceptance_tests: the sustainability verdict is tested against r minus g sensitivity bands
rollover and maturity profile checked

nodes.definition: Reads how anchored or unanchored inflation expectations are and how central-bank credibility shapes the inflation process.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: divergence between survey and market expectations or a de-anchoring signal

pros.claim: anchored expectations make inflation self-correcting
pros.example: credible inflation targets kept 2022 expectations broadly anchored

cons.claim: expectation measures disagree and can de-anchor nonlinearly
cons.example: ignoring market breakevens understated tail inflation risk

acceptance_tests: survey and market measures are cross-checked
de-anchoring thresholds defined

nodes.definition: Reads money aggregates the real vs nominal interest rate and the neutral rate r-star as context for the monetary stance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: velocity instability or an r-star re-estimate

pros.claim: the real rate vs r-star shows whether policy is tight or loose
pros.example: a real rate below r-star flagged a loose stance despite a high nominal rate

cons.claim: money-aggregate signals are unstable and velocity shifts
cons.example: M2 growth mis-signaled inflation in periods of velocity collapse

nodes.definition: Reads nominal and real exchange rates pass-through to prices and regime choice fixed float peg and its constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: regime change large depreciation or a pass-through coefficient shift

pros.claim: pass-through links currency moves to domestic inflation
pros.example: sharp depreciations fed import-price inflation in emerging markets

cons.claim: pass-through is nonlinear and regime-dependent
cons.example: assuming low pass-through understated inflation after a peg break

acceptance_tests: regime constraints checked against the trilemma
pass-through stated with horizon

nodes.definition: Reads the trade and current-account balance via the saving-investment identity and external imbalance signals.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a balance-of-payments revision or terms-of-trade shock

pros.claim: the saving-investment identity frames deficits as saving-investment gaps not just trade
pros.example: twin-deficit logic linked fiscal and external balances

cons.claim: the accounting identity can mask causal direction
cons.example: reading a deficit as pure competitiveness loss ignored capital-inflow drivers

nodes.definition: Reads cross-border capital flows sudden-stop risk reserve adequacy and external financing pressure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sudden-stop signal reserve-adequacy breach or external-debt repricing

pros.claim: flow reversals trigger crises faster than trade adjustment
pros.example: sudden-stop framing explained rapid emerging-market crises

cons.claim: gross flows and valuation effects are volatile and hard to monitor
cons.example: net-only flow reads missed gross funding fragility

acceptance_tests: reserve adequacy checked against external short-term debt
gross and net flows both examined

nodes.definition: Reads how historical international monetary regimes gold standard Bretton Woods floating constrain adjustment and crises.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new historical evidence or an analogy-misuse signal

pros.claim: history shows regime tradeoffs between credibility and flexibility
pros.example: Eichengreen linked gold-standard rigidity to Depression severity

cons.claim: historical analogies can be misapplied to different structures
cons.example: gold-standard analogies misread modern fiat constraints

nodes.definition: Reads the slack-inflation relationship Phillips curve its flattening and expectations-augmented dynamics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence of a Phillips-curve slope change or nonlinear steepening

pros.claim: it ties real slack to inflation integrating labor gap and expectations
pros.example: a flat Phillips curve explained muted pre-2020 inflation despite low unemployment

cons.claim: the curve is unstable flat and possibly nonlinear
cons.example: relying on a flat curve understated 2022 inflation when it steepened

acceptance_tests: slope reported with uncertainty
the expectations term is included explicitly

nodes.definition: Assesses vintage revision and real-time data reliability so reads are not built on data that later changes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a large benchmark revision or seasonal-adjustment method change

pros.claim: it guards against decisions built on heavily revised early estimates
pros.example: real-time output-gap errors stemmed from preliminary GDP later revised

cons.claim: real-time reliability is hard to quantify ex ante
cons.example: treating advance estimates as final caused premature policy reads

nodes.definition: Integrates aggregates cycle policy and external reads into a coherent falsifiable macro state narrative with confidence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any upstream block read materially changes or a scenario is falsified

pros.claim: it forces internal consistency across blocks and a falsifiable read
pros.example: reconciling the supply-shock and Phillips reads produced one coherent 2022 narrative

cons.claim: integration can launder weak block reads into false confidence
cons.example: a confident narrative built on a fragile output-gap estimate misled

acceptance_tests: the narrative states falsification conditions
block conflicts are explicitly reconciled
a confidence grade is attached

edges.why_related: scoped question selects which output aggregates matter
edges.risk_of_conflict: building accounts before scoping wastes effort
edges.example: horizon tag decides real vs nominal GDP focus
edges.resolution_rule: scope frame dominates; finalize scope before accounts

edges.why_related: scope sets which price index and horizon are relevant
edges.example: core vs headline choice follows the scoped question
edges.resolution_rule: scope frame dominates index selection

edges.why_related: scope decides whether slack matters for the question
edges.example: cyclical question prioritizes slack over structural labor
edges.resolution_rule: scope frame dominates

edges.why_related: gap needs actual output from the accounts
edges.risk_of_conflict: gap without solid GDP is unstable
edges.example: real GDP feeds the gap numerator
edges.resolution_rule: accounts dominate; lock GDP before gap

edges.why_related: dating uses output as a coincident indicator
edges.example: GDP declines feed turning-point calls
edges.resolution_rule: accounts dominate the dating input

edges.why_related: leading-indicator validation needs a phase reference
edges.example: inversion lead time is measured against dated recessions
edges.resolution_rule: dating provides the reference frame

edges.why_related: shock classification reads the price side
edges.risk_of_conflict: shock calls without prices are blind
edges.example: price-output co-movement needs the inflation read
edges.resolution_rule: inflation read precedes shock typing

edges.why_related: the stance responds to the inflation read
edges.example: above-target inflation justifies tightening
edges.resolution_rule: inflation read drives the stance

edges.why_related: fiscal stance is read against the gap
edges.risk_of_conflict: stance without the gap conflates cycle and policy
edges.example: the cyclically-adjusted balance needs the gap
edges.resolution_rule: gap precedes stance reading

edges.why_related: multiplier application needs the fiscal impulse
edges.risk_of_conflict: multipliers without an impulse are abstract
edges.example: the impulse scales the multiplier
edges.resolution_rule: stance read precedes multiplier sizing

edges.why_related: sustainability needs the primary-balance path from fiscal
edges.example: the primary balance enters the debt dynamics
edges.resolution_rule: fiscal read feeds the sustainability identity

edges.why_related: pass-through is read against domestic inflation
edges.risk_of_conflict: FX inflation effect needs a price base
edges.example: import-price pass-through adds to domestic inflation
edges.resolution_rule: inflation read grounds pass-through

edges.why_related: the external balance uses the saving-investment identity from the accounts
edges.risk_of_conflict: external read without accounts is unanchored
edges.example: net exports are a GDP component
edges.resolution_rule: accounts feed the external identity

edges.why_related: flow pressure is read against the exchange-rate regime
edges.risk_of_conflict: flows without regime miss the trilemma
edges.example: a peg under outflows forces reserve loss
edges.resolution_rule: FX regime conditions the flow read

edges.why_related: the Phillips relation needs the gap as the slack input
edges.risk_of_conflict: Phillips without the gap lacks a slack measure
edges.example: the gap is the slack variable in the curve
edges.resolution_rule: gap read feeds the Phillips slack term

edges.why_related: the synthesis integrates the shock read
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesis without shock sign is incoherent
edges.example: the supply-demand split shapes the whole narrative
edges.resolution_rule: shock read feeds synthesis

edges.why_related: the synthesis integrates the policy stance
edges.example: the stance frames the inflation-path narrative
edges.resolution_rule: policy read feeds synthesis

edges.why_related: shocks change the level and persistence of inflation
edges.example: a supply shock raised 2022 headline inflation
edges.resolution_rule: attribute inflation to the dominant shock with stated persistence

edges.why_related: policy tightening lowers demand and the output gap with a lag
edges.example: rate hikes cool the gap over several quarters
edges.resolution_rule: apply the transmission lag before reading the gap effect

edges.why_related: fiscal changes scaled by the multiplier move the gap
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong multiplier misstates the gap effect
edges.example: a high-multiplier package narrows a recessionary gap
edges.resolution_rule: scale fiscal impulse by the state-dependent multiplier

edges.why_related: currency moves change import prices and inflation via pass-through
edges.example: a depreciation raised tradable-goods inflation
edges.resolution_rule: add pass-through to the inflation attribution

edges.why_related: expectations feed into realized inflation through price-setting
edges.example: de-anchored expectations sustained a wage-price spiral
edges.resolution_rule: weight expectations in the inflation-persistence read

edges.why_related: tightening monetary and loosening fiscal pull demand opposite ways
edges.example: fiscal stimulus into a hiking cycle blunts disinflation
edges.resolution_rule: monetary dominance for price stability unless fiscal sustainability is at risk

edges.why_related: higher policy rates fight inflation but worsen debt dynamics
edges.example: rate hikes raised debt-service and stressed r-g
edges.resolution_rule: price stability dominates short run; flag fiscal-dominance risk for review

edges.why_related: closing the gap to support employment can raise inflation
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-weighting one mandate distorts the read
edges.example: running the economy hot lifted inflation
edges.resolution_rule: balance per mandate weights; escalate when both breach thresholds

edges.why_related: defending the currency can conflict with the domestic rate needed for inflation
edges.example: rate cuts for growth pressured a fragile peg
edges.resolution_rule: domestic price stability dominates under a float; peg defense dominates under a hard peg

edges.why_related: free capital flows constrain exchange-rate and rate autonomy via the trilemma
edges.example: open capital accounts forced a peg abandonment
edges.resolution_rule: pick two trilemma corners; document the sacrificed objective

edges.why_related: stimulus exploiting high multipliers can worsen debt sustainability
edges.example: large multipliers justified spending that strained debt
edges.resolution_rule: sustainability dominates when fiscal space is exhausted

edges.why_related: data revisions bound how confidently the gap can be read
edges.example: revised GDP flipped a real-time gap sign
edges.resolution_rule: cap gap confidence by the revision-risk estimate

edges.why_related: index methodology and revisions bound the inflation read
edges.example: seasonal-adjustment changes shifted measured inflation
edges.resolution_rule: qualify inflation reads by methodology and revision risk

edges.why_related: the monetary regime constrains the available debt-adjustment mechanisms
edges.example: a gold-standard-style regime barred monetization
edges.resolution_rule: constrain the sustainability options by the regime

edges.why_related: knowing the cycle phase should precede shock interpretation
edges.example: a recession context reframed a shock as demand-driven
edges.resolution_rule: date the phase before finalizing shock sign

edges.why_related: forward signals should inform the stance read sequencing
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring lead signals delays the read
edges.example: an inversion prompted earlier easing debate
edges.resolution_rule: consider lead signals before finalizing the stance read

edges.why_related: an incoherent synthesis can trigger rescoping of the question
edges.example: a contradictory narrative forced a horizon change
edges.resolution_rule: revisit scope only when synthesis conflicts are material; stop after two rescopes

edges.why_related: synthesis contradictions can trigger shock re-classification
edges.example: a narrative mismatch reopened the supply-demand split
edges.resolution_rule: reclassify only on material new evidence; stop after two passes

edges.why_related: credibility shifts can prompt revisiting historical-regime analogies
edges.example: a credibility shock reopened a regime-history comparison
edges.resolution_rule: revisit history only on regime-relevant credibility shifts; cap at one revisit

edges.why_related: both are demand-management policy levers read in parallel
edges.example: both are assessed for their effect on aggregate demand
edges.resolution_rule: use for joint policy-mix framing not substitution

edges.why_related: both proxy economic slack from different angles
edges.example: both feed an overheating assessment
edges.resolution_rule: use for cross-checking slack not as duplicates

conflict_axes.trigger: closing the gap to support jobs raises inflation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: follow the stated mandate weights; when both breach thresholds escalate to human review
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: both inflation and unemployment breach target bands simultaneously
conflict_axes.example: running the economy hot lifted employment and inflation together

conflict_axes.trigger: monetary and fiscal levers pull demand in opposite directions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: monetary dominance for price stability unless fiscal sustainability is threatened
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: fiscal stimulus materially offsets a disinflation campaign
conflict_axes.example: a stimulus package during a hiking cycle blunted disinflation

conflict_axes.trigger: rate hikes that fight inflation worsen debt dynamics
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: price stability dominates in the short run; escalate when rollover stress appears
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: debt-service jump threatens rollover at current rates
conflict_axes.example: rate hikes raised debt-service and stressed the r-g path

conflict_axes.trigger: fixed rate, free capital, and autonomous policy cannot all hold
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: under a float domestic price stability dominates; under a hard peg defense dominates
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: open capital account forces abandoning either the peg or rate autonomy
conflict_axes.example: open capital flows forced a peg abandonment

conflict_axes.trigger: the same inflation can be read as supply-driven or demand-driven
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: let price-output co-movement decide the sign; escalate when the call drives a major policy pivot
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the supply-demand split would flip the recommended policy direction
conflict_axes.example: the 2021-22 debate over whether inflation was supply or demand driven

conflict_axes.trigger: high-multiplier stimulus can erode debt sustainability
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: sustainability dominates once fiscal space is exhausted
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: stimulus pushes the debt path beyond a sustainable r-g
conflict_axes.example: large multipliers justified spending that strained the debt path

conflict_axes.trigger: acting on timely but revisable data trades speed for reliability
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reliability dominates for irreversible decisions; timeliness may dominate for reversible ones
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an irreversible policy choice rests on heavily revisable data
conflict_axes.example: advance GDP estimates later revised flipped a real-time gap sign

conflict_axes.trigger: a mechanical rule conflicts with judgment about novel shocks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the rule benchmark anchors the read; document and escalate large discretionary deviations
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the recommended stance deviates materially from the rule benchmark
conflict_axes.example: a novel supply shock justified deviating from a Taylor-rule prescription

conflict_axes.trigger: a historical analogy may not fit the current structure
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: structural comparability dominates; down-weight or drop poorly fitting analogies
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an analogy is invoked despite a material structural mismatch
conflict_axes.example: gold-standard analogies misapplied to a modern fiat regime

edge_cases.trigger: a nominal series is compared to a real one
edge_cases.example: nominal GDP growth mistaken for real growth during high inflation
edge_cases.detection_method: check that deflator treatment is consistent across compared series
resolution: flag the conflation in the read

edge_cases.failure_mode: supply inflation labeled demand causes over-tightening
edge_cases.example: treating a supply shock as demand led to excess tightening
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the shock sign against price-output co-movement

edge_cases.trigger: an end-of-sample filtered gap is taken as final
edge_cases.failure_mode: spurious gap sign drives a wrong stance
edge_cases.example: a real-time gap flipped sign after GDP revision
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the real-time gap to a revised-vintage gap
resolution: report the gap with a revision band

edge_cases.trigger: a flat-curve assumption is applied during steepening
edge_cases.example: relying on a flat curve understated 2022 inflation
edge_cases.detection_method: test slope stability against recent data and expectations
resolution: re-estimate slope with the expectations term

edge_cases.trigger: a permanently low r is assumed
edge_cases.failure_mode: rollover risk is understated when rates rise
edge_cases.example: assuming low r understated rollover risk when rates rose
edge_cases.detection_method: stress the r-g path across rate scenarios

edge_cases.trigger: low pass-through is assumed after a regime break
edge_cases.detection_method: test pass-through against the regime and recent FX moves

edge_cases.trigger: an indicator signal is treated as a confirmed turning point
edge_cases.failure_mode: a false positive triggers a premature call
edge_cases.example: an inversion signal misfired in a soft-landing episode
edge_cases.detection_method: require corroboration before acting on a single lead signal

edge_cases.trigger: advance estimates are treated as final for an irreversible decision
edge_cases.failure_mode: a decision rests on data that later changes
edge_cases.example: treating advance estimates as final caused a premature policy read
edge_cases.detection_method: tag each input with its vintage and revision risk
resolution: wait for a firmer vintage or hedge

edge_cases.trigger: an accounting identity is read as a causal claim
edge_cases.example: reading a deficit as pure competitiveness loss ignored capital drivers
edge_cases.detection_method: separate the identity from the behavioral causal claim

edge_cases.trigger: all three trilemma objectives are assumed simultaneously
edge_cases.example: assuming peg, open capital, and rate autonomy together produced inconsistency
edge_cases.detection_method: check the policy set against the trilemma corners

edge_cases.trigger: a confident narrative rests on fragile block reads
edge_cases.example: a confident narrative built on a fragile gap estimate misled
edge_cases.detection_method: trace narrative confidence back to weakest-block confidence
resolution: cap narrative confidence at the weakest block

workflow.objective: type the macro question and select the aggregate set
acceptance_tests: question type horizon and nominal real status are explicit
exit_criteria: aggregate shortlist maps to the question
workflow.do_first_because: scope frames every downstream aggregate and policy read and is high coupling

acceptance_tests: headline inflation decomposed into core and volatile
GDP reported in consistent real terms
exit_criteria: aggregates are internally consistent with the scope
workflow.do_first_because: aggregates are the measurement foundation all later reads depend on

workflow.objective: assess vintage and revision risk of the aggregates
acceptance_tests: each aggregate input is tagged with a vintage and revision-risk estimate
exit_criteria: reliability flags attached to each aggregate
workflow.do_first_because: reliability must be known before reads are built so confidence is not over-claimed

workflow.objective: estimate the output gap with an uncertainty band
acceptance_tests: the gap is reported with an explicit uncertainty band and method
workflow.do_first_because: the gap is a high-risk, high-coupling input to shocks, policy, and Phillips

workflow.objective: date the cycle phase and read forward signals
acceptance_tests: lead signals require corroboration before a turning-point call
exit_criteria: phase label and lead signals are consistent
workflow.do_first_because: the cycle phase conditions shock and policy interpretation

workflow.objective: classify the dominant shock as supply or demand with persistence
acceptance_tests: the shock sign is justified by price-output co-movement
persistence horizon stated
exit_criteria: shock sign is consistent with the gap and inflation reads
workflow.do_first_because: shock sign is high-risk and pivots the policy direction

workflow.objective: read the policy stance and mix against the cycle and expectations
acceptance_tests: the stance is judged against a rule benchmark
expectations are cross-checked across measures
exit_criteria: stance and mix are internally consistent
workflow.do_first_because: the policy stance is high-risk and drives the inflation-path narrative

workflow.objective: read debt sustainability and the external block
acceptance_tests: the sustainability verdict is tested against r-g sensitivity bands
the external policy set is checked against the trilemma
exit_criteria: debt and external reads are consistent with the policy stance
workflow.do_first_because: debt and external risks are high-irreversibility and constrain feasible policy

workflow.objective: integrate slack, expectations, and inflation via the Phillips linkage
entry_criteria: gap, slack, expectations, and inflation available
acceptance_tests: the slope is reported with uncertainty and includes the expectations term
exit_criteria: the linkage is consistent with the shock and policy reads
workflow.do_first_because: the linkage reconciles labor, gap, and inflation before final synthesis

workflow.objective: integrate all blocks into a falsifiable macro narrative with a confidence grade
entry_criteria: all block reads available and reviewed
acceptance_tests: the narrative states falsification conditions
block conflicts are explicitly reconciled
confidence is capped at the weakest block
exit_criteria: narrative is coherent, falsifiable, and human-reviewed before any hard lock
workflow.do_first_because: synthesis is the capstone and must not hard-lock before human review and validation pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk read could be finalized quickly without checks
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for high-risk-if-wrong reads
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests before finalizing the read
dominance_rules.example: a fast shock call was held for price-output verification

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks its prerequisite reads
dominance_rules.required_action: finalize prerequisites before the dependent node
dominance_rules.example: synthesis waited for the shock and policy reads

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks eligible evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: label all estimates heuristic and avoid false precision
dominance_rules.example: a heuristic gap estimate was not presented as measured

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is ready to lock but failed a check
dominance_rules.required_action: resolve the failed check before any lock
dominance_rules.example: a debt verdict failed its r-g sensitivity test and was not locked

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision is being automated
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation at risk and irreversibility thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: escalate to human review before the decision
preserve the schema and trim content instead
dominance_rules.example: weak similarity edges were dropped to keep counts safe

dominance_rules.trigger: prose quality competes with strict JSON validity
dominance_rules.required_action: emit strict JSON and move prose into fields
dominance_rules.example: explanatory text was kept inside defined fields only

dominance_rules.required_action: cite SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR or exclude the claim
dominance_rules.example: no observed labels were used without data

dominance_rules.trigger: a local optimization reorders work badly
dominance_rules.required_action: follow the anti-rework order even if locally slower
dominance_rules.example: reliability was assessed before reads were built

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing implies a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker link to sequence or feedback
dominance_rules.example: a synthesis-to-scope link was modeled as feedback not dependency

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not measure aggregates before the question is scoped
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unscoped aggregates select the wrong series and force rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: aggregate work begins with no scoped question
anti_rework_rules.example: building real GDP before deciding the horizon wasted effort

anti_rework_rules.rule: assess data reliability before building reads on it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reads on unreliable data get redone after revisions
anti_rework_rules.example: a gap built on advance GDP was redone after revision

anti_rework_rules.rule: estimate the output gap before classifying shocks
anti_rework_rules.rationale: shock sign without the gap output side gets reclassified
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a shock is classified with no gap input
anti_rework_rules.example: a demand call was reversed once the gap was added

anti_rework_rules.rationale: shock sign without the price side is unstable
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a shock is classified with no inflation read
anti_rework_rules.example: a shock sign flipped after the inflation decomposition

anti_rework_rules.rule: read expectations before judging the monetary stance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a stance ignoring anchoring misjudges urgency and is redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a stance is set with no expectations read
anti_rework_rules.example: a stance was revised once de-anchoring was detected

anti_rework_rules.rule: read the fiscal stance before judging debt sustainability
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a sustainability verdict without the primary balance is hollow
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a debt verdict cites no primary-balance path
anti_rework_rules.example: a verdict was redone after the cyclically-adjusted balance was added

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not synthesize before all block reads are reviewed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a premature synthesis is redone when a block read changes
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: synthesis runs with unreviewed block reads
anti_rework_rules.example: a narrative was rewritten after the gap was revised

anti_rework_rules.rule: define formula variables before computing scores
anti_rework_rules.rationale: scores computed from undefined variables are inconsistent and redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a score has no backing derivation inputs
anti_rework_rules.example: derived fields were recomputed from explicit inputs

anti_rework_rules.rule: map conflict axes before writing dominance rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dominance rules without conflicts are ungrounded and rewritten
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a dominance rule names no conflict
anti_rework_rules.example: the policy-mix rule referenced the policy-mix axis

anti_rework_rules.rule: run acceptance tests before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before tests forces an expensive unlock and revalidation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock is requested with unrun tests
anti_rework_rules.example: the synthesis was held in soft_lock until human review

iteration_protocol.detection: validator report shows a failed check
acceptance_tests: all failed checks are enumerated

iteration_protocol.detection: defect list has more than one item
action: rank defects by risk and downstream impact
acceptance_tests: queue ordered by risk-adjusted impact

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: defect node has cross_topic_coupling at or above 0.75
action: trace downstream nodes and edges affected
acceptance_tests: impact set lists all affected dependents

iteration_protocol.detection: top of the defect queue is non-empty
action: route the defect to its repair owner
acceptance_tests: the fix resolves the targeted check
the previously failed check now passes and no new failures appear

iteration_protocol.detection: an input metric or label changed
acceptance_tests: recomputed scores satisfy the formulas within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible conflict is unresolved
iteration_protocol.detection: an unresolved axis exceeds the risk threshold
action: escalate to human review with a decision record
acceptance_tests: a decision record with approver is produced
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: the conflict is resolved or formally accepted

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
action: compare counts, formula consistency, and references against the prior version
acceptance_tests: no mandatory check regressed versus the prior version
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no regression versus the prior version

test_cases.input_summary: scope a single inflation question and read core vs headline
tightening monetary while loosening fiscal under high debt
large depreciation under open capital account
advance GDP later revised flips the gap sign

version_increment_rules: increment on any node or edge semantic change
increment on formula or threshold change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade to draft on upstream dependency change
